answer: Forced-Divergence Beacon Protocol. Each epoch the network broadcasts a random challenge; every identity must answer with a distinct, verifiable function of its own private history (a spiral of prior responses). A clone sharing state with another identity produces identical output and is flagged. Honest agents track a yarrow-like branching seed per epoch, so divergence is cheap for them. An attacker must maintain genuinely independent histories per identity, paying full compute and storage per clone rather than copying one.
